slides.title: Welcome to Uniquem
slides.caption: Welcome to Uniquem. Safety is everyone's job here. Follow your manager's direction, and if you're ever unsure about a task, stop and ask.

slides.title: No smoking anywhere on Uniquem property
slides.caption: There is no smoking anywhere on Uniquem property, inside or outside, including the doors, loading docks, trailers and parking lot. Our products and their vapours can catch fire. Put it out, and only smoke off the property.

slides.title: Forklifts: make eye contact
slides.caption: When you see a forklift, stop and wait. Make eye contact with the driver before you move. Drivers stop and confirm they have seen you too.

slides.title: Steel-Toe Boots Required
slides.caption: Our warehouse runs forklifts and power jacks every day. Steel-toe boots are required at all times when you are in the warehouse.

slides.title: Know Your Fire Extinguishers and Exits
slides.caption: Know where the nearest fire extinguisher, fire alarm and exits are, and keep them clear. Never block them with pallets, totes or drums.

quiz.q: You are not sure how to do a task on site. What should you do?
options: Work it out on your own
quiz.explanation: Always follow your manager's direction. When in doubt, stop and ask.

quiz.q: Where on Uniquem property is smoking allowed?
options: Outside by the warehouse back door
By the trailers at the loading dock
quiz.explanation: No smoking anywhere on Uniquem property, inside or out. Put it out and only smoke off the property.

quiz.q: A forklift is coming toward you in the warehouse. What do you do?
options: Stop, wait and make eye contact with the driver before you move
quiz.explanation: Stop and make eye contact so the driver knows you are there. Only move once the driver has stopped and seen you.

quiz.q: What do you keep clear of pallets, totes and drums?
options: The nearest fire extinguisher, fire alarm and exits
quiz.explanation: Know where the nearest fire extinguisher, fire alarm and exits are, and keep them clear.

slides.title: Our Docks and Trucks
slides.caption: We have 3 docks and two kinds of trucks: containers and trailers.

slides.title: Talk to the Driver First
slides.caption: Before anyone goes into a trailer, talk to the driver and make sure the truck is stopped and parked.

slides.title: Check the Trailer Is Stable
slides.caption: Check if the truck is still hooked to the trailer. If the trailer stands alone, make sure its jacks are far enough to the front. If not, place our own jacks under the trailer before going in.

slides.title: Light On, Dock Plate Set
slides.caption: Trailers have no lights inside. Before you go in, swing the dock light into the trailer and turn it on so you can see everything. Then set the dock plate so it sits flat and secure on the trailer floor.

slides.title: Entering with Equipment
slides.caption: Before you drive a forklift into a trailer, double check that your seatbelt is buckled. If you're using a power jack, only one power jack goes into the trailer at a time.

slides.title: Can't See? Drive Backwards
slides.caption: If you're carrying two stacked totes or pallets and can't see in front of you, never drive forward. Always drive backwards and look in the direction you're travelling.

slides.title: Wrap Up with the Driver
slides.caption: When loading is done, remove the dock plate from the trailer. Then go talk to the driver, hand over the proper shipping paperwork, and give them the placards required for the load.

quiz.q: How many docks do we have?
quiz.explanation: We have 3 docks.

quiz.q: What must you do before entering a trailer?
options: Talk to the driver and make sure the truck is stopped and parked
quiz.explanation: Talk to the driver and make sure the truck is stopped and parked before anyone goes into the trailer.

quiz.q: The trailer is not hooked to a truck and its jacks aren't far enough forward. What do you do?
options: Place our own jacks under the trailer before going in
Ask the driver to hold it
quiz.explanation: If the trailer stands alone and its jacks aren't far enough forward, place our own jacks under the trailer before going in.

quiz.q: What should you do before going into a dark trailer?
options: Turn on the dock light and point it into the trailer
Go in slowly without a light
Ask the driver to turn on the trailer lights
quiz.explanation: Trailers have no lights inside. Swing the dock light into the trailer and turn it on before you go in.

quiz.q: What must a forklift operator do before driving into a trailer?
options: Double check the seatbelt is buckled
Raise the forks all the way up
Drive in fast to save time
quiz.explanation: Double check the seatbelt is buckled before driving a forklift into a trailer.

quiz.q: You're carrying two stacked totes and can't see in front of you. What do you do?
options: Drive backwards, looking where you're going
Lean out to the side and drive forward
Ask someone to walk in front of you
quiz.explanation: If you can't see in front of you, drive backwards and look in the direction you're travelling.

quiz.q: What do you give the driver when loading is done?
options: The shipping paperwork and the required placards
Just the keys to the dock door
Nothing, the driver handles the paperwork
Only a verbal OK to leave
quiz.explanation: Hand over the shipping paperwork and the placards required for the load.

slides.title: Pre-Shift Check
slides.caption: Before every shift, check the forks, tires, horn, lights, brakes and battery charge, and make sure there are no leaks.

slides.title: Seatbelt On, Every Time
slides.caption: Put your seatbelt on every time, even for short trips.

slides.title: Corners and Blind Spots
slides.caption: Slow down and sound the horn at corners, doorways and blind spots.

slides.title: Slow and Steady
slides.caption: Keep to a slow, steady speed, and no sharp turns.

slides.title: Carry Loads Low
slides.caption: Carry loads low, about 10 to 15 cm off the floor, with the mast tilted back.

slides.title: Can't See? Drive Backwards
slides.caption: If the load blocks your view, drive backwards and look in the direction of travel.

slides.title: Know Your Capacity
slides.caption: Never go over the rated capacity, and keep the load centered on both forks.

slides.title: Make Eye Contact
slides.caption: Make eye contact with people walking before moving near them.

slides.title: No Riders, Ever
slides.caption: Forklifts are for one person only. Never let anyone ride along, not even for a short trip.

slides.title: Stay Inside the Cab
slides.caption: Keep your arms, hands and feet inside the cab at all times.

slides.title: Ramps: Load Uphill
slides.caption: Go up and down ramps with the load facing uphill.

slides.title: Park It Right
slides.caption: When parking, lower the forks flat on the floor and set the brake.

slides.title: Pre-Use Check
slides.caption: Before using the power jack, check the handle, brakes, horn, battery and forks.

slides.title: Walk Beside or Behind
slides.caption: Walk beside or behind the power jack, never in front of it when pulling a load.

slides.title: Don't Get Pinned
slides.caption: When pulling the power jack, never trap yourself between the jack and a wall or object behind you. Keep at least 3 feet of space behind you.

slides.title: Corners: Slow and Horn
slides.caption: Go slowly around corners and sound the horn so others know you're coming.

slides.title: One Jack in the Trailer
slides.caption: Only one power jack in a trailer at a time. Wait on the dock until the trailer is clear.

slides.title: No Riding
slides.caption: Never ride on the power jack, and don't let anyone else ride on it either.

slides.title: Park It Right
slides.caption: When you're done, lower the forks fully to the floor and turn the power jack off.

quiz.q: How high off the floor do you carry a forklift load?
options: As high as the mast goes
quiz.explanation: Carry loads low, about 10 to 15 cm off the floor, with the mast tilted back.

quiz.q: The load blocks your view. What do you do?
options: Drive backwards and look in the direction of travel
Raise the load so you can see under it
quiz.explanation: If the load blocks your view, drive backwards and look in the direction of travel.

quiz.q: Who can ride on a forklift?
quiz.explanation: Forklifts are for one person only. Never let anyone ride along.

quiz.q: How do you travel on a ramp with a load?
options: As fast as the ramp allows
quiz.explanation: Go up and down ramps with the load facing uphill.

quiz.q: How do you park a forklift?
options: Leave it running in the aisle
Lower the forks flat on the floor and set the brake
quiz.explanation: When parking, lower the forks flat on the floor and set the brake.

quiz.q: Where do you walk when pulling a load with a power jack?
options: In front of the power jack
Beside or behind the power jack
quiz.explanation: Walk beside or behind the power jack, never in front of it when pulling a load.

quiz.q: How much space do you keep behind you when pulling a power jack?
quiz.explanation: Never trap yourself between the jack and a wall. Keep at least 3 feet of space behind you.

quiz.q: How many power jacks can be in a trailer at one time?
quiz.explanation: Only one power jack in a trailer at a time. Wait on the dock until the trailer is clear.

quiz.q: Can you ride on a power jack?
options: Yes, if you stand on the forks
No. Never ride on it, and don't let anyone else ride on it
quiz.explanation: Never ride on the power jack, and don't let anyone else ride on it either.

quiz.q: What do you do when you are done with the power jack?
options: Lower the forks fully to the floor and turn it off
Leave it on in the aisle
quiz.explanation: When you're done, lower the forks fully to the floor and turn the power jack off.

slides.title: Coverall On, Every Time
slides.caption: Wear your coverall every time, because chemicals can spill or splash.

slides.title: Strong Odour? Mask On
slides.caption: Wear a mask or respirator when a product has a strong odour or gives off fumes.

slides.title: Use the Suction Arm
slides.caption: Pull the suction arm over the opening of the drum, tote or pail so fumes are drawn away before they reach you.

slides.title: Never Leave a Mixer Running
slides.caption: Watch high-speed mixers and low-speed blenders at all times, and never leave one running unattended.

slides.title: Know Your Eyewash Station
slides.caption: Know where the nearest eyewash station is before you start work.

slides.title: Follow the Batch Sheet
slides.caption: Never mix chemicals that weren't meant to go together. Follow the batch sheet exactly.

slides.title: Hands Clear of the Mixer
slides.caption: Keep hands, tools and loose clothing away from a running mixer, and stop it fully before adding anything or reaching in.

slides.title: Spill? Clean It and Report It
slides.caption: If something spills, grab the spill kit, soak it up with absorbent pads, and tell your supervisor right away.

slides.title: Keep It Clean and Clear
slides.caption: Keep your area clean. Coil and hang up hoses and cords so nothing is left across the walkway.

slides.title: Wash Up, No Food or Drink
slides.caption: Wash your hands after handling chemicals and before breaks, and never bring food or drink into the production area.

slides.title: Lift Smart
slides.caption: Lift pails by the handle using your legs, not your back. Never lift drums or totes by hand; use the power jack or forklift.

slides.title: Not Even One Drip
slides.caption: Fill drums, totes and pails carefully with no spills at all. If anything spills or drips, even a single drop, clean it up right away, not later. We keep our work area spotless.

quiz.q: When do you wear your coverall?
options: Every time, because chemicals can spill or splash
Only if your supervisor is watching
quiz.explanation: Wear your coverall every time, because chemicals can spill or splash.

quiz.q: A product has a strong odour or gives off fumes. What do you wear?
quiz.explanation: Wear a mask or respirator when a product has a strong odour or gives off fumes.

quiz.q: Where do you put the suction arm?
options: Over the opening of the drum, tote or pail
quiz.explanation: Pull the suction arm over the opening so fumes are drawn away before they reach you.

quiz.q: Can you leave a mixer running while you step away?
options: Yes, if it is almost done
No. Never leave a mixer or blender running unattended
quiz.explanation: Watch mixers and blenders at all times, and never leave one running unattended.

quiz.q: When do you need to know where the eyewash station is?
options: At the end of the shift
Only if you wear a mask
quiz.explanation: Know where the nearest eyewash station is before you start work.

quiz.q: Two chemicals are not on the batch sheet. What do you do?
options: Mix a small amount to test
Follow the batch sheet and do not mix them
Ask a coworker to mix them
Add them if the colour looks right
quiz.explanation: Never mix chemicals that weren't meant to go together. Follow the batch sheet exactly.

quiz.q: You need to add something to a running mixer. What do you do first?
options: Stop it fully before adding anything or reaching in
Toss it in from a distance
quiz.explanation: Stop the mixer fully before adding anything or reaching in.

quiz.q: Something spills. What do you do?
options: Grab the spill kit, soak it up, and tell your supervisor
quiz.explanation: Grab the spill kit, soak it up with absorbent pads, and tell your supervisor right away.

quiz.q: A single drop spills while you fill a pail. What do you do?
options: Leave it until the end of the shift
Wipe it only if it is a big spill
quiz.explanation: If anything spills or drips, even a single drop, clean it up right away. We keep our work area spotless.

quiz.q: How do you move a drum?
options: Lift it by hand with a coworker
Use the power jack or forklift
Tip it and roll it by yourself
quiz.explanation: Never lift drums or totes by hand. Use the power jack or forklift.
